messages:
sylvia: flagging a canary regression after kernel-selector v2.4 landed. ingress p99 climbed 36ms -> 70ms, sys CPU +19% around 02:14 UTC. small requests seem worst.
omar: :eyes: grabbing traces. initial look shows a big increase in writev syscall count during tokenization/proxy handoff.
jin: kvcache metrics show async flush queue depth up and hot-shard evictions spiking. looks like many tiny fragments now causing index churn.
sylvia: sanitized log:
```
INGRESS recv stream
tokenizer: emit 48B chunk
proxy: writev([hdr,48B,ctl]) -> flush
kernel: sys_writev x3
```
sylvia: previously proxy coalesced to ~1KB writes; selector v2.4 biases ultra-low-latency kernels and reduced batching window.
lucy: flamegraph: https://perf.redwood/internal/fg/3456789012 shows tokenize->writev->epoll wait loop.
perf-bot: nightly diff: https://ci.redwood/pipelines/9802/diff/3456789012 (regression flagged).
omar: short-term mitigation: flip runtime flag proxy.coalesce_stream_ms=8 on canary to re-enable small-write coalescing per-stream.
jin: bench: proxy.coalesce_stream_ms=8 -> writev count -65%, ingress p99 -> 42ms, kvcache hot-evict -38%. added numbers to PR.
sylvia: rollout plan: flip on 15% canary at 3456789050, monitor ingress_p99, sys_cpu, kvcache.hot_evictions for 15m. rollback if p99 > 75ms or error% increases >0.4%.
lucy: long-term idea: teach kernel-selector to accept a "batch_tolerance" hint so flows with high write density prefer kernels that tolerate slightly longer batching windows.
omar: alternative medium-term: tokenizer.min_emit_size=128 to reduce syscall frequency, but that bumps tokenizer CPU slightly; tradeoff needs evaluation.
jin: adding temporary alert: kvcache.hot_evictions > 5/s during the canary window.
sylvia: doing the flip now. will post snapshots and rollback steps to #incidents if anything spikes. tagging @omar and @jin for post-roll analysis.
